lines.trans: Fedya, when will the sea bream finally be ready?
The receipt was punched only now, I am rushing!
Guests at the table ate all the bread!
And what can I do right now?
Waiters have been waiting for hot fish for forty minutes!
We have a regular fishermen convention today!
Fedya, calm down and hand over urgent orders!
I am doing everything possible, do not yell.
Wait, what is this terrible stench?
Oh no, the quails on the stove burnt!
What a nightmare, complete smoke in the kitchen!
Urgently take the pan off the hot fire!
The new shift began with pure disaster.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
сделать всё возможное = do everything possible

examples.text: Марина, я делаю всё возможное! Послушай, ты несправедлива!
examples.trans: Marina, I'm doing everything possible! Listen, you're being unfair!

examples.text: Я делаю всё возможное, не кричи.
examples.trans: I am doing everything possible, do not yell.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stench', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Подожди, что это за страшная вонь?
examples.trans: Wait, what is this terrible stench?
She will raise a stink on the internet.

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Abstract masculine noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-ость', denoting the quality or state of 'guest'.

examples.trans: All the guests love them very much.

examples.text: Сегодня вечером к нам придут гости.
examples.trans: Guests are coming to our place tonight.

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'sea bream', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: When will the sea bream finally be ready?

examples.text: Федя, когда дорада наконец будет готова?
examples.trans: Fedya, when will the sea bream finally be ready?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'smoke' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Где мы? Кругом дым и воронки.
examples.trans: Where are we? Smoke and bomb craters are all around.

examples.text: Какой кошмар, на кухне полный дым!
examples.trans: What a nightmare, complete smoke in the kitchen!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'подождать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to expect') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Declinable masculine noun meaning 'order', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: In the kitchen they are preparing this order.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'catastrophe, disaster' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for us!

examples.text: Это просто катастрофа для нашей кампании!
examples.trans: This is simply a catastrophe for our campaign!

examples.text: О нет, это катастрофа для кухни!
examples.trans: Oh no, this is a disaster for the kitchen!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'when'.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда ты наконец принесёшь горячий соус на раздачу?
examples.trans: When will you finally bring the hot sauce to the pass?

meanings.note: colloquial: Это кошмар! = That's awful / a nightmare!

examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue.

examples.text: Это кошмар, я не спорю. Но зачем на видео снимать?
examples.trans: That's a nightmare, I don't argue. But why film it on video?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to shout', forming an aspectual pair with 'крикнуть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Не надо кричать. Хорошо, я буду сегодня.
examples.trans: There's no need to shout. All right, I'll be there tonight.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец').

examples.text: О, наконец тепло! Слава богу. Сейчас ещё чай сделаю.
examples.trans: Oh, it's warm at last! Thank goodness. Now I'll make some tea too.

начаться.gloss: to begin, to start, to break out

meanings.en: to begin, to start, to break out (intransitive)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start, to break out', paired with 'начинаться'.

examples.trans: The film started at seven sharp.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'fire', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Срочно снимай сковороду с горячего огня!
examples.trans: Urgently take the pan off the hot fire!

meanings.en: to hand over, give back, yield
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'давать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hand over, give back'.

examples.text: Тимур, не наглей и отдавай товар!
examples.trans: Timur, don't get cheeky and hand over the goods!

examples.text: Федя, успокойся и отдавай срочные заказы!
examples.trans: Fedya, calm down and hand over urgent orders!

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'quail', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The quails on the stove burnt!

examples.text: О нет, перепела на плите сгорели!
examples.trans: Oh no, the quails on the stove burnt!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'stove', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('slab') (large flat stone or concrete block) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно смотри за температурой на плите.
examples.trans: Watch carefully the temperature on the stove.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Ладно, включай плиту и доставай мясо!
examples.trans: All right, turn on the stove and get the meat!

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to wait', forming an aspectual pair with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'full' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('complete, total, utter') (полный кошмар = a total nightmare) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'бить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to punch', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробивать'.

examples.trans: The receipt was rung up just now!

examples.text: Чек пробили только сейчас, я спешу!
examples.trans: The receipt was punched only now, I am rushing!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'fisherman', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Fishermen found him on the bottom.

examples.text: Рыбаки потом нашли его на дне.
examples.trans: Fishermen later found him on the riverbed.

examples.text: У нас сегодня прямо съезд рыбаков!
examples.trans: We have a regular fishermen convention today!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

сгореть.gloss: to burn down, to burn up

meanings.en: to burn up, to be destroyed by fire
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'гореть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to burn down', forming an aspectual pair with 'сгорать'.

examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned.

examples.text: А трава в мешках сгорела. Из-за вас!
examples.trans: And the herbs in the sacks burned. Because of you!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'today'.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'frying pan', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('skillet') (shallow cooking pan) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Я сниму сковороду с горячей плиты вовремя.
examples.trans: I will remove the pan from the hot stove on time.

examples.text: Рыба почти готова на горячей сковороде.
examples.trans: The fish is almost ready on the hot pan.

meanings.note: morning or afternoon shift at school or work

examples.trans: We're on the afternoon shift today.

examples.text: А у нас сегодня вторая смена.
examples.trans: We're on the afternoon shift today.

снимать.gloss: to take off; to film; to rent

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нимать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to take off', forming an aspectual pair with 'снять'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to film, to photograph') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('to rent') (снимать квартиру) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Watch. I'm taking off my ring.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: сорок рублей; other cases: сорока

examples.trans: I don't know. Forty, I think.

спешить.gloss: to hurry, be in a rush

meanings.en: to hurry, rush, be in a hurry
meanings.note: куда ты спешишь? = where are you rushing to?

examples.trans: What happened? Where are you rushing to?
We are in a big hurry for the train.
Wait a bit, Sokolov. Do not hurry.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('urgent, pressing').

examples.trans: This is a very urgent matter.

examples.text: Яков Григорьевич, у меня срочный вопрос к вам.
examples.trans: Yakov Grigoryevich, I have an urgent question for you.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'terrible' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('nothing serious') ('ничего страшного') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Теперь мы одна команда.
examples.trans: Nothing serious. Now we're one team.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'convention', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: У нас сегодня прямо съезд рыбаков!
examples.trans: We have a regular fishermen convention today!

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ъесть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to eat', forming an aspectual pair with 'есть'.

examples.text: Скоро. А пока я есть хочу, слона бы съел!
examples.trans: Soon. But for now I'm hungry, I could eat an elephant!

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.
plural хлеба, stressed on the ending
plural хлеба, stressed on the ending

examples.trans: The bread is on the table.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'receipt' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня чек есть! Вот он, смотрите.
examples.trans: I have a receipt! Here it is, look.

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean
Secondary conversational sense ('pure') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
